# Research

My research interests sit at the intersection of biomedical engineering, experimental physiology
and instrumentation.

## Current research

### Ex vivo liver viability with ICG-NIR

The Master's thesis integrates:

- Ex vivo organ perfusion.
- Hemodynamic and thermal monitoring.
- Baseline physiological characterization.
- Biomedical optics and NIR fluorescence.
- ICG kinetic analysis.
- Quantitative functional assessment.

[View the full thesis project →](projects/thesis.qmd)

## Research approach

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Physiological problem"] --> B["Measurable variables"]
    B --> C["Literature + requirements"]
    C --> D["Prototype"]
    D --> E["Instrumentation"]
    E --> F["Experiment"]
    F --> G["Validation"]
    G --> H["Iteration / integration"]
```

I use scientific literature not only as theoretical background, but also as an engineering
resource for geometries, materials, dimensions, physiological ranges, measurement methods and
validation criteria.

## Areas of interest

- Organ perfusion and preservation.
- Biomedical instrumentation.
- Biosensors.
- Biomedical optics.
- NIR fluorescence.
- Medical imaging.
- Signal processing.
- Medical devices.
- Neuroengineering.
- Robotic rehabilitation.
